items.readme_text: # Alien [![X (formerly Twitter) Follow](https://img.shields.io/twitter/follow/alien)](https://x.com/alien) [![GitHub Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/alienplatform/alien)](https://github.com/alienplatform/alien/releases) [![Slack](https://img.shields.io/badge/Slack-Join-4A154B?logo=slack&logoColor=white)](https://alien.dev/slack) **Infrastructure for software outside your cloud.** Some of your product has to run where you don't control the infrastructure: a customer's AWS, Google Cloud or Azure account, their Kubernetes cluster, or a site with no internet access at all. Alien runs that piece there (the data plane) and keeps it connected to your control plane: releases roll out on their own, logs come back, and your backend can call into it, all over connections the environment opens outbound. The manager is the center of it. Run it yourself from this repository, or let [alien.dev](https://alien.dev) run it for you. The same `alien` CLI works with both. ## Quickstart Install the CLI: ```bash curl -fsSL https://alien.dev/install | sh ``` ### With alien.dev ```bash alien login alien init && cd alien alien dev # run the app locally, no cloud account needed alien release # build and publish a release alien onboard acme --allow @acme.com --platforms kubernetes ``` The [Quickstart](https://alien.dev/docs/quickstart) walks through it. ### With your own manager Start a manager. It prints an admin API key the first time: ```bash docker run -d --name alien-manager -p 8080:8080 -v alien-data:/data \ -e BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080 \ ghcr.io/alienplatform/alien-manager docker logs alien-manager ``` Point the CLI at it, release your app, and onboard a customer: ```bash alien login --manager http://localhost:8080 --token ax_admin_... alien release alien onboard acme --platforms kubernetes --secret-input accessToken=... ``` `alien onboard` prints a token for the customer and the commands their Kubernetes admin runs once. Their cluster pulls the chart and images from your manager with that token, which stays out of shell history: ```bash read -rs ALIEN_TOKEN # paste acme's token, then Enter printf '%s' "$ALIEN_TOKEN" | helm registry login manager.example.com --username acme --password-stdin printf 'management:\n token: %s\n' "$ALIEN_TOKEN" | \ helm install files oci://manager.example.com/charts/files \ --namespace files --create-namespace \ --set management.name=acme \ --timeout 15m \ --values values.yaml \ --values - ``` For real customers, run the manager where their clusters can reach it over HTTPS: with the [Helm chart](infra/helm/alien-manager/) on Kubernetes, the [Terraform module](infra/aws-ecs-manager/) on Amazon ECS, or `docker run` on any machine. See [Self-hosting](https://alien.dev/docs/self-hosting). ## How it works ``` Your cloud Customer environment ┌──────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────────┐ │ alien CLI your │ │ Operator │ │ │ backend │ outbound │ ├─ deploys each release │ │ ▼ │ │ HTTPS │ ├─ ships logs and traces │ │ Manager ◀─────┘ ◀──────┼─────────────┼── └─ updates itself │ │ │ │ │ │ │ ▼ │ │ │ │ OpenTelemetry backend │ │ Your containers, storage │ └──────────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────────────┘ ``` Alien deploys in two ways: - **Push.** The customer grants a narrowly scoped role in their cloud account, and the manager deploys through the cloud's APIs. - **Pull.** The customer runs the Operator: a Helm chart on Kubernetes, or a container in their cloud. It connects outbound to the manager, fetches releases and deploys them locally. Nothing listens for inbound connections. Both give you the same things: releases, heartbeats, logs and commands. See [How Alien works](https://alien.dev/docs/how-alien-works). ## Define your app ```typescript import * as alien from "@alienplatform/core" // The customer's S3-compatible bucket, supplied at install time. const bucket = new alien.Storage("bucket").build() const api = new alien.Container("api") .code({ type: "source", src: ".", toolchain: { type: "rust", binaryName: "api" } }) .cpu(0.5) .memory("512Mi") .port(8080) .link(bucket) .permissions("api") .build() export default new alien.Stack("files") .platforms(["kubernetes"]) .add(bucket, "frozen") .add(api, "live") .permissions({ profiles: { api: { bucket: ["storage/data-read", "storage/data-write"] } } }) .build() ``` The same resources map to each platform's native services: Storage becomes S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, or an S3-compatible store (MinIO, Ceph) on Kubernetes. Workers, queues, key-value stores and vaults work the same way. See [Infrastructure](https://alien.dev/docs/infrastructure). ## After one install Once a customer installs, you don't need access to their environment again: - **Releases.** `alien release` rolls out to every deployment following its channel (`production` by default). Stage releases on other channels, promote them with `alien releases promote`, and pin a deployment with `alien deployments pin`. The Operator also updates itself to the version the manager runs. - **Images.** Clusters pull images through the manager with their deployment token. No registry credentials to hand out. - **Logs and traces.** Deployments send OpenTelemetry to the manager, which forwards it to your backend: Datadog, Grafana, Honeycomb, Axiom, Coralogix, or any OTLP endpoint. `alien logs --deployment acme/acme` shows recent logs without one. - **Commands.** Invoke handlers inside a deployment from your backend with [Remote Commands](https://alien.dev/docs/commands). ## Air-gapped environments Sites with no connection to your manager get the same app through one folder their admin carries in and out. You keep running `alien release`; the site runs `alien-deploy sync` on both sides of the gap: ```bash alien onboard site-7 --platforms kubernetes --airgapped # the site's token, bundle key and start command # online: sends the site's reports, downloads the next signed update into site-7-sync/ alien-deploy sync --token ax_... --manager https://manager.example.com # inside the site: verifies the signature, pushes images to the site's registry, # installs or upgrades the chart, writes a report for the trip back alien-deploy sync --registry registry.internal/vendor -f values.yaml \ --trusted-key ed25519:... # first install only; later updates must match it ``` After the first run, `alien-deploy sync` with no options does whatever the side it runs on can do. Updates carry only the image layers the site doesn't have, reports carry the site's state and logs (none are lost between trips), and `alien-deploy rollback` returns to the previous release. See [Air-gapped deployments](https://alien.dev/docs/deploying/air-gapped). ## Least-privilege permissions Alien derives the permissions each part needs from the stack definition: - **Provisioning.** The customer's admin sets up the environment once with their own credentials. Alien never holds these. - **Management.** What Alien uses day to day. Frozen resources only get health checks. Live resources can be updated, but management never includes data access. - **Application.** What your code can reach, as declared in permission profiles. `storage/data-read` becomes `s3:GetObject` on AWS, `storage.objects.get` on Google Cloud and the matching Azure role. See [Permissions](https://alien.dev/docs/permissions) and [Frozen and live](https://alien.dev/docs/frozen-and-live). ## Examples - [customer-kubernetes](examples/customer-kubernetes): a service in your customers' Kubernetes clusters, including air-gapped ones, from a manager you host - [remote-worker-ts](examples/remote-worker-ts): tool execution inside the customer's cloud for an AI agent - [data-connector-ts](examples/data-connector-ts): query private databases without sharing credentials - [webhook-api-ts](examples/webhook-api-ts): an API inside the customer's network More in [examples/](examples/). ## Repository | Path | What it is | |------|------------| | [`crates/alien-cli`](crates/alien-cli) | The `alien` CLI | | [`crates/alien-manager`](crates/alien-manager) | The manager | | [`crates/alien-operator`](crates/alien-operator) | The Operator that runs in pull-mode environments | | [`crates/alien-deploy-cli`](crates/alien-deploy-cli) | `alien-deploy`, run by a customer's admin | | [`packages/`](packages) | TypeScript SDKs | | [`infra/`](infra) | Helm chart and Terraform for running the manager, and cloud modules it uses | ## Documentation - [Quickstart](https://alien.dev/docs/quickstart) - [How Alien works](https://alien.dev/docs/how-alien-works) - [Self-hosting](https://alien.dev/docs/self-hosting) - [Kubernetes](https://alien.dev/docs/deploying/kubernetes) - [Observability](https://alien.dev/docs/observability) - [Remote commands](https://alien.dev/docs/commands) ## Community - [Slack](https://alien.dev/slack): help and feedback - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/alienplatform/alien/issues): bugs and feature requests - [X](https://x.com/alien): updates

items.name: eta
items.description: Eta is a self-contained 0-vendor multi-agent all-in-one endomorphic agent loop/runtime/harness/app.
items.readme_text:
Who's holding the AI that knows you?

100% transparent. 100% yours.
An open-source workbench for always-on agents that run on your machine, answer with your own model accounts, and keep everything they know in one SQLite file you can open.

TL;DR · What it is · The part where we disagree · Install · Documentation · License

## TL;DR Grok Bot says every agent gets its own computer. True. That computer sits in xAI's datacenter. Muse gets your mail, your photos, your shopping. Today gets your calendar, your meetings, your work chat, and promises the memory is "readable, editable, erasable" — on their servers, on their word. Grok Bot, Muse, Today: different logos, the same trade. They learn everything about you, and they keep it somewhere you will never be allowed to look. **We don't think you have to accept the second half.** eta is the same product with the address changed. The thing that knows you lives on the machine under your desk. Read its source, watch what it does, swap the model, open the database, carry the whole thing to another machine with `cp -r`. > One process. One SQLite file. Zero required external services. 100% BYOK. ## What it is A workbench where one person directs a crew of always-on agents: each one has a persona, a project it belongs to, its own tools and its own memory. You talk to them, hand them tasks, put things on a schedule — and when something needs your OK, they stop and wait for it. Long jobs survive the conversation that started them; wake-ups arrive only with what's new since the last time the agent looked. Nothing here is a black box, because there is no box: - **Every agent has its own computer — and it's yours.** Run the host on your laptop and the sessions run there. Add a second machine and the sessions move: the daemon dials out to you, shows a fingerprint, and waits for you to approve it. - **100% BYOK, not "supports BYOK".** Your ChatGPT, Grok and Gemini subscriptions by device code, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and the private model in your own rack. A first-class citizen, not a compatibility mode. Nothing is routed anywhere you didn't point it. - **Memory is a SQLite file.** One file, in the same data directory as everything else, queried per conversation. Open it, grep it, fix a row, delete a row. Delete it and it's actually gone. - **You can see the work.** Every turn and every tool call — what it read, what it ran, what it changed — lands on a timeline instead of a spinner. When an agent wakes up, it gets the increment, not a rewrite of the whole story. - **Nothing to cancel.** No seat, no credits, no rate limit we invented. There is no account to be banned from, because there is no account. - **The door has a lock that turns itself on.** Bind anything other than loopback and the token gate comes up on its own. A file on disk, mode 0600, `Authorization: Bearer` for scripts. And it's all there to change. Prompts are files, personas are markdown cards, tools are plugins, the wire is documented frame by frame. If the runtime doesn't behave the way you need, it's not a feature request away — it's right there. ## The part where we disagree **Grok Bot** Every agent gets its own computer — in their datacenter, on their dynamic router, which conveniently never tells you which model actually answered. **Muse** Ten million users in forty days, and the most popular thing to do with it is shopping. It's not a workbench, it's a storefront that remembers your address. **Today** "Memory you can read, edit and erase." Great. Ship me the file, then. **Claude Code** Useful? Yes. Yours? Not really. **Codex** The prompt, the state, the context and the storage move around while you're expected to smile and trust the dashboard. **OpenCode** If the runtime ignores your plan, that isn't autonomy, it's an argument you keep losing. ## Install There are two ways to run eta. **We recommend installing the host** on a computer that stays on — a home server, a desktop, a small VPS. Your agents keep working while your laptop is closed, and you reach the same eta from any browser or your phone. ### Recommended: install the host eta is one file, `eta-host`. It serves the web app, keeps everything in `~/.eta`, and needs nothing else running. Builds for Linux x64, macOS (Apple silicon) and Windows x64 are on [Releases](https://github.com/0xfe-project/eta/releases/latest). On Linux: ```sh curl -LO https://github.com/0xfe-project/eta/releases/latest/download/eta-host-linux-x64 chmod +x eta-host-linux-x64 mkdir -p ~/.local/share/eta/host mv eta-host-linux-x64 ~/.local/share/eta/host/eta-host ~/.local/share/eta/host/eta-host install-service --host tailscale ``` That starts eta now and at every login, listening on your tailnet; leave out `--host` to keep it on this machine only. On a headless box, `loginctl enable-linger` keeps it running without a login. Open `http://:8787`. Anything other than localhost turns on a token by itself: the first visit is `http://:8787/?token=`, with the token from `~/.eta/access-token`. On macOS, use `eta-host-darwin-arm64` the same way, and clear the download flag before the first run (`xattr -d com.apple.quarantine eta-host-darwin-arm64`): the build is not signed yet. On Windows, download `eta-host-windows-x64.exe` and run `eta-host-windows-x64.exe install-service` in an Administrator terminal. It runs as a Windows service under your account and asks for your password once, which it hands to Windows without storing it. To try it without installing anything, run the file directly (`./eta-host-linux-x64`): eta runs in that terminal until you stop it. ### Experimental: the desktop app Prefer to just open an app? Download the desktop installer for your system from [Releases](https://github.com/0xfe-project/eta/releases), open it, choose **Run on this computer**, and it sets everything up by itself. > The desktop app is experimental. eta runs only while the app is open and the computer is awake, and > other devices can't reach it. For an assistant that is always there, install the host on a server > instead — the app can connect to that host too (**Connect to an existing host**). ## First steps Settings → Model services → Add a source: sign in with a ChatGPT or Grok subscription, or paste an API key. Then create an agent and start a conversation. ## Updating Settings → Update, or `eta-host upgrade`. It verifies the download, waits for working agents, backs up the database to `~/.eta/backups`, restarts the service, and goes back to the old version on its own if the new one does not start. The machines you added follow on their next connect. ## More machines Sessions can run on other computers too. Settings → Machines → Add a machine gives you a command to run there; it shows a fingerprint, and the machine joins once you approve it. See [Self-hosting](docs/self-hosting.md#more-machines-the-daemon). ## Documentation - [Self-hosting](docs/self-hosting.md): flags, the token, reverse proxies, more machines, upgrades - [Development](docs/development.md): the layout, working from a checkout, checks - [Release](docs/release.md): how versions are built and published, checksums - [Architecture](docs/architecture/overview.md): processes, the wire protocol, data, access control ## License eta is under the [MIT License](LICENSE). What it carries from others keeps its own terms: the Eta Sans font is not covered by the MIT License, and a compiled host embeds SearXNG, which is AGPL-3.0-or-later. See [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

items.name: TemporalStore
items.description: Open-source Rust TemporalStore for LLM context management, temporal features, and risk control
items.readme_text: # TemporalStore **Open-source Rust storage for online features, LLM context, and control state.** Feature serving and LLM context are equally important, first-class workloads. Serve latest values, long histories, high-cardinality aggregates, WindowReduce features, frequency caps, and agent memory in one engine. Context ingestion, retrieval, ranking, token-budgeted packing, APIs, and SDKs are in TemporalStore. **Apache-2.0, available worldwide for use, modification, commercial deployment, and contributions under the license.** [Documentation](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/tree/main/docs) | [Issues](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/issues) ## Implementation entry points **On this page:** [Quick start](#quick-start) | [Use cases](#use-cases) | [Recorded benchmarks](#recorded-benchmark-highlights) | [Durability](#architecture-and-durability) | [Deployment boundaries](#deployment-boundaries) | [Contributing](#build-and-contribute). | Area | Start reading | |---|---| | Native Feast provider and supported online-store behavior | [Provider guide](integrations/feast/feast_temporalstore_command/README.md) | | Storage engine composition | [Engine module](crates/temporalstore-rust/src/engine.rs) | | Write-ahead log implementation | [WAL module](crates/temporalstore-rust/src/wal.rs) | The provider guide separates latest values, optional history, aggregates, and tracked teardown. Enabling one path does not establish the throughput or storage cost of the others; choose the API and acknowledgement policy before measuring a workload. ## Use cases | Workload | What you can build | Start here | |---|---|---| | **Feast online serving** | Materialize features and retrieve current entity values through Feast, with explicit timestamp, expiry, and acknowledgement policies | [Feast integration](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/tree/main/integrations/feast) | | **Latest features and profiles** | User/item profiles, lookup features, hashes, and online state for recommendation, search, ads, and personalization | [One-cluster architecture](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/TEMPORALSTORE_ONE_CLUSTER_TEMPORAL_FEATURES.md) | | **Long-sequence features** | Recent clicks, sessions, interactions, and typed behavior histories; timestamp-window reads and count-based retention | [Sequences and aggregates](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/blog_feature_sequences_and_aggregates.md) | | **High-cardinality features** | Separate user-item, user-category, user-author, device, or campaign histories; exact windowed count, sum, average, min/max, and first/last | [Aggregate example](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/feature_aggregate_high_cardinality_example.md) | | **WindowReduce Features** | Merge cell samples, reduce member statistics over a time window, and rank candidates by counts, ratios, or weighted scores | [Window Reducer model](#windowreduce-features), [worked example](docs/WINDOW_REDUCE_WORKED_EXAMPLE.md) | | **Control state** | Set/get online state, atomic single-key counters, quotas, pacing, suppression, and risk/fraud decisions | [Control-state guide](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/blog_control_state_frequency_caps.md) | | **Frequency caps** | Per-user, campaign, or placement exposure limits using windowed counters | [Frequency-cap guide](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/blog_control_state_frequency_caps.md) | | **LLM context and agent memory** | Conversations, resources, entities, reusable memory, retrieval, and token-budgeted context assembly | [Context guide](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/context_management_on_temporalstore.md) | | **Collections, blobs, and streams** | Membership/deduplication, sorted sets, lists, multipart blobs, range reads, and batch/stream ingestion | [Command surface](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/redis_compatibility_matrix.md) | ### Feast API support The [native Feast provider](integrations/feast/feast_temporalstore_command/README.md) is an online store and materialization target, not an offline training store. | API or workflow | Support | |---|---| | `get_online_features` and its async form | Latest-value serving through bounded compact projections; compatible views share entity planning. | | `online_write_batch` and its async form | Materialization with timestamp suppression, optional TTL, and bounded requests; atomic timestamp checks apply to the eligible latest-only route. | | `query_feature_aggregate` / `query_feature_aggregates` | Provider extensions for retained history; numeric reducers require integer features and the selected history layout. | | Precomputed vector read/write | Store and fetch vector-valued features; this does not provide provider vector search. | | `update` / `teardown` | Schemaless updates and tracked cleanup; exact teardown requires key tracking before materialization. | Feast async calls change client scheduling, not the node's persistence policy. See [latency, amplification, and allocation choices](integrations/feast/feast_temporalstore_command/README.md#latency-amplification-and-allocations) before comparing latest-only serving, history queries, or another backend. Provider vector-search hooks and offline point-in-time retrieval are not implemented here. ### Configure Feast Start the data node with the [quick start](#quick-start). From this checkout, install Feast and enable the native provider on Python's import path: ```bash pip install feast msgpack export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/integrations/feast${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}" ``` In your existing Feast repository, keep its project, registry, provider, entity definitions, and offline sources. Set its `feature_store.yaml` online-store block: ```yaml online_store: type: feast_temporalstore_command.TemporalStoreCommandOnlineStore host: 127.0.0.1 port: 17102 shard_id: 1 max_batch_commands: 512 max_write_batch_commands: 4096 max_batch_request_bytes: 4194304 skip_dedup: false adaptive_timestamp_prefetch: true key_ttl_seconds: null write_feature_history: false track_keys_for_teardown: false ``` Use the reachable data-node address and assigned shard for your deployment. The configuration above selects latest-value serving without history, expiry, or teardown tracking. Set a positive `key_ttl_seconds` to enable whole-key expiry; enable `track_keys_for_teardown` before writing if exact cleanup is required. History and tracking add storage work and can change the write route. Run Feast's normal workflow from that repository, with the provider import path still exported: ```bash feast apply feast materialize-incremental "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S)" ``` Read using `FeatureStore(repo_path=".").get_online_features(...)` with your registered feature names and entity rows. TemporalStore serves the materialized online values; Feast's configured offline source and materialization engine remain responsible for loading them. Async API calls do not relax the node's durability policy. See the [provider configuration and API guide](integrations/feast/feast_temporalstore_command/README.md) for history, aggregates, async calls, older-node behavior, and cleanup limits. ### Choose a Feast materialization path Use the [native provider guide](integrations/feast/feast_temporalstore_command/README.md) to configure these independently; enabling latest-value serving does not enable them all. | Requirement | Configuration and consequence | |---|---| | Reject stale latest-value updates | Keep `skip_dedup: false`; common latest-only, shared-layout conditional routes compare timestamps and mutate under one server shard guard. | | Expire entity state | Set `key_ttl_seconds`; rejected stale rows do not refresh expiry on the conditional TTL route. | | Retain feature history | Enable `write_feature_history`; this adds writes and uses a different path from latest-only materialization. | | Enumerate keys during teardown | Enable `track_keys_for_teardown` before materializing; without tracking, teardown cannot enumerate existing rows. | | Reduce serialization for mostly stale batches | Keep `adaptive_timestamp_prefetch: true`; a per-thread routing hint can add a fresh timestamp pre-read, while eligible survivors still use server-side conditional writes. | History, tracking, mixed layouts, and older-node fallbacks can use a separate timestamp-read and write sequence. That fallback is not an atomic conditional update across concurrent writers. `skip_dedup: true` disables stored-timestamp suppression; out-of-order materialization can then replace newer values. The native provider defaults to 4,096 write commands per request, also bounded by 4 MiB of encoded data; reads retain the 512-command response bound. A caller batch can therefore span several requests, not one atomic transaction. Measure the selected history, tracking, TTL, and acknowledgement configuration separately, including maintenance and retained WAL bytes, not just accepted rows per second. Eligible synchronous shared-row writes now leave cold packed payloads out of the payload cache until a read requests them. Updates to an already cached frame can refresh it eagerly, using one lookup of the first selected field rather than a scan of the projection. This reduces write-side copying without increasing the cache budget; cold reads can instead fetch and decompress a WAL group. Set `TS_HASH_WRITE_AROUND=0` before startup to retain eager admission. Async, bulk, replay, consensus-apply, and memory-limited paths keep their existing behavior. Location registration and durability barriers are unchanged. See [indexed WAL reads and cache admission](docs/indexed_wal_reads.md) for eligibility and memory costs; compare mixed reads and writes, not write QPS alone. ### WindowReduce Features The Window Reducer (WindowReduce) is a cell-based model within Feature. It stores timestamped samples of members, labels, and numeric lanes. Writes merge lanes with declared reducers. `WindowReduceRank` selects a window, filters, reduces per member, scores, returns bounded top-k, and projects fields; it can also restrict the members it reads, end a trailing window at the newest stored sample, guarantee members in chosen lanes, and score by a decayed sum. `WindowReduceFanInRank` ranks the merged cells of several keys and `WindowReduceRankBatch` answers several independent reads in one request. `WindowReduceRollup` folds old samples into coarser time buckets and can cap each label group, so a key written every minute does not keep every sample. A retried write carries a token, so sending it twice does not count it twice. Build engagement rankings, conversion rates, and multi-signal features alongside scalar aggregates, with explicit schema and query bounds. The vocabulary is small. Nothing in the engine knows what the names mean; a deployment declares them once, in the header its first write carries, and every later write is checked against that header. | Term | Meaning | |---|---| | **Window Reducer** (WindowReduce) | The model: samples of cells under one key, merged by lane reducers on write and reduced over a time window on read. | | **Entity** and **dimensions** | An entity (a `u64`, text or bytes) plus up to eight named dimensions become one stored feature key, so a read by those values is one lookup. | | **Sample** | The set of cells stored at one timestamp of that key. | | **Cell** | A **member** (an id or bytes), up to four named `u64` **labels**, and one to sixteen named `i64` **lanes**. | | **Lane reducer** | The verb that merges two values of a lane for one member: `Sum`, `Max`, `Min`, `First`, `Last` or `Count`. | #### Use cases Each scenario below is exercised by a test named in the last column. | Scenario | How the Window Reducer is used | Test | |---|---|---| | **Per-user engagement counters by channel and content kind** | Entity = user; dimensions = `channel`, `kind`; members = items shown; lanes = `impressions`, `clicks` (both `Sum`). Writes at the same timestamp merge into one sample and the receipt says what was created and what merged. | `a_worked_example_of_window_reduce` | | **Per-item rolling ratios** | `WindowReduceRank` over `Last { duration_ms: 60_000 }` reduces each item across the window and scores it by `Ratio` (click rate) or `Wilson` (a lower confidence bound that does not trust a rate seen once). In the example the two scores order the same three items oppositely. | `a_worked_example_of_window_reduce` | | **Best items for a placement** | A predicate on a label (`slot < 3`) cuts cells before a member's samples are reduced, then the read ranks the rest. | `a_worked_example_of_window_reduce` | | **Rolling history compacted into coarser buckets** | `WindowReduceRollup` with `older_than_ms` and `bucket_ms` folds minute samples into one sample per hour. Each lane folds by its own verb: summed lanes add, a `Max` lane keeps the peak, a `Last` lane keeps the newest value. Rolling an already-rolled bucket again changes nothing. | `a_worked_example_of_a_rollup` | | **Bounded member sets per label** | The rollup's optional cap keeps the best `keep` cells of each label group, scored like a ranked read, so a long-lived key does not grow without bound. | `a_worked_example_of_a_rollup` | | **Ranking inside a chosen set of members** | A member set on the read: `include` names the members to read and `exclude` those to leave out (exclusion wins), applied before a member's samples are reduced. Used for "rank these candidates" and "rank everything except what was already shown". | `a_member_set_changes_the_answer_exactly_as_an_independent_fold_says` | | **A window that follows the data, not the clock** | `anchor: newest` ends a `Last` window at the newest stored sample, so a key whose writes stopped (a paused or replayed feed) reads the same whenever it is read. | `an_anchored_window_reads_the_newest_sample_whatever_the_clock_says` | | **Guaranteed minimum per lane** | A quota keeps at least so many members with a non-zero `clicks` value among the top-k, even when the best-ranked members have none. It never returns more than `top_k` rows. | `a_quota_selects_exactly_as_a_fold_of_the_ranking_says` | | **Recency-weighted scores** | `Decay { lane, half_life_ms }` scores a member by its stored values, each halved for every half-life of age from the newest sample of the window. No clock is read. | `a_decay_score_answers_its_hand_computed_value_live_and_after_a_restart` | | **One question over several keys** | When `channel` is a dimension, "the best items for this user over every channel" spans keys. `WindowReduceFanInRank` merges the cells of up to 64 keys before it scores, so the answer is the one a single key holding all their samples would give. | `a_worked_example_of_a_ranked_read_across_the_channels_of_one_user` | | **Several independent reads in one request** | `WindowReduceRankBatch` carries up to 64 reads, each with its own key and spec, and answers them in request order; one failing read fails no other. | `a_batch_of_reads_answers_each_as_the_single_read_would_in_request_order_and_one_failing_read_fails_no_other` | | **A write that can be sent twice** | A merge-reduce append may carry a `retry_token`. The same token on the same key answers the first receipt with `replayed` set and writes nothing; a key remembers its last 16 tokens. | `a_repeated_token_answers_the_first_receipt_and_writes_nothing`, `the_ring_holds_sixteen_through_the_engine_and_the_seventeenth_token_evicts_the_first` | | **Rolling history in tiers** | The rollup fold accepts an ordered list of tiers, finest first: recent history stays at a fine bucket and older history gets a coarser one, with an optional catch-all that folds everything older into one sample at stamp 0. Today this is the pure function inside the crate; its command is not on `main` yet (see In progress). | `a_tiered_rollup_equals_an_independent_fold_with_a_bucket_per_tier` (unit test, `engine::window_reduce_rollup::tier_tests`) | | **Multi-signal features from one key** | One header can declare up to sixteen lanes with different reducers (counts, maxima, latest values), read back together in one ranked read with `Weighted` scores. | `a_window_reduce_rollup_is_a_command`, `a_window_reduce_ranked_read_is_a_command` | The tests are in `crates/temporalstore-rust/src/engine/tests/`. The write, read and rollup walk-throughs, with the numbers each step produces, are in [Window Reducer: merged, windowed, ranked statistics](docs/WINDOW_REDUCE_WORKED_EXAMPLE.md). #### Commands | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `FeatureAppendWithPolicy` with `MergeReduce` | Merges the request's cells into the sample stored at each point's timestamp, lane by lane. Answers a receipt: samples written, cells created, cells merged. Mismatch with the stored header is refused naming the differing field. | | `WindowReduceRank` | Window (`Between`, `Last`, `Since`, `LastN`, `NewestRows`), named predicates over labels, lanes or `member`, a score (`Lane`, `Ratio`, `Wilson`, `Member`, `Time`, `Weighted`, `Decay`), `top_k`, and optional projected fields. Optional controls, left out of the encoding when unused: a member set (`members`: `include`, `exclude`), an `anchor` (`request` or `newest`), and a `quota`. A name the key does not declare is refused. | | `WindowReduceFanInRank` | The same read over up to 64 keys that share one spec. The cells of every key are merged before they are scored; the answer says how many keys held a sample in the window. Keys are read on one shard. | | `WindowReduceRankBatch` | Up to 64 independent reads, each with its own key and spec, answered in request order. A read that cannot be served answers with its reason and fails no other. | | `WindowReduceRollup` | Folds every sample stamped strictly before `older_than_ms` into `bucket_ms` buckets (cells merge by member, oldest first) and optionally caps each group. Answers samples and cells before and after, and cells dropped. A rollup that would change nothing writes nothing. | | `WindowReduceRemove` | Removes cells from one key by time window (stamps, inclusive), member set (include and exclude) and predicates over a label, a lane or `member`, at most 8, ANDed. Answers samples before and after, cells in the window, and cells removed. A sample left with no cell is removed; a request that restricts nothing is refused and one that matches nothing writes nothing. | The shape of each request, copied from the tests: ```rust // Write: merge cells into the sample at a timestamp. Command::FeatureAppendWithPolicy { key: key.to_string(), points: vec![FeaturePoint { timestamp_ms, value: encode_value(&header(), cells).unwrap() }], policy: FeatureWritePolicy::MergeReduce, retry_token: None, // Some(token) makes a resend answer the first receipt } // Read: rank the last minute by click rate. Command::WindowReduceRank { key: key.to_string(), spec: WindowReduceRankSpec { window: WindowReduceWindow::Last { duration_ms: 60_000 }, filters, score: WindowReduceScore::Ratio { numerator: "clicks".to_string(), denominator: "impressions".to_string() }, top_k: 10, project: Vec::new(), members: CellMemberFilter::default(), anchor: WindowReduceAnchor::Request, quota: WindowReduceQuota::default(), }, } // The same read, narrowed: only these members, none of those, the window ends at the newest // stored sample, and at least two members with a click are guaranteed a place. let narrowed = WindowReduceRankSpec { members: CellMemberFilter { include: Some(vec![CellMemberId::U64(1), CellMemberId::U64(2), CellMemberId::U64(3)]), exclude: vec![CellMemberId::U64(2)], }, anchor: WindowReduceAnchor::Newest, quota: WindowReduceQuota { lanes: vec![WindowReduceLaneQuota { lane: "clicks".to_string(), count: 2 }], others: 0 }, ..WindowReduceRankSpec::new( WindowReduceWindow::Last { duration_ms: 60_000 }, WindowReduceScore::Lane { lane: "impressions".to_string() }, 10, ) }; // Recency-weighted: clicks halved for every 10 minutes of age from the newest sample. let decayed = WindowReduceScore::Decay { lane: "clicks".to_string(), half_life_ms: 600_000 }; // One question over every channel of one user: the keys are merged before they are scored. Command::WindowReduceFanInRank { keys: vec![email_key.clone(), push_key.clone(), feed_key], spec: narrowed.clone() } // Independent reads, answered in request order. Command::WindowReduceRankBatch { queries: vec![ WindowReduceRankBatchItem { key: email_key.clone(), spec: narrowed.clone() }, WindowReduceRankBatchItem { key: push_key, spec: narrowed }, ], } // Roll old samples into hours, keeping the best item of each slot. Command::WindowReduceRollup { key: key.to_string(), spec: WindowReduceRollupSpec { older_than_ms: hour, bucket_ms: hour, cap: Some(WindowReduceCapSpec { group_by: Some("slot".to_string()), score: WindowReduceScore::Ratio { numerator: "clicks".to_string(), denominator: "impressions".to_string() }, keep: 1, }), }, } ``` #### Limits A request over a limit is refused, not truncated. | Limit | Value | |---|---| | Dimensions per key, labels per cell, lanes per cell | 8, 4, 16 | | Member bytes, entity bytes, text dimension bytes | 256 each | | Field name bytes | 64 | | Cells per point of a write request, cells per sample | 1,024, 4,096 | | Cells in all the points of one merge-reduce command | 262,144 | | `top_k` | 1,000 | | Samples in one ranked window | 512 (a wider window is refused, not truncated) | | Predicates per read, lanes in a `Weighted` score | 8, 8 | | Members in a read's `include` set, and in its `exclude` set | 1,024 each, as sent | | Lanes in a quota, members a quota reserves (lane counts plus `others`) | 16, 1,000 | | Half-life of a `Decay` score | 1 ms to ten years | | Keys, samples and cells in one fan-in read | 64, 1,024, 262,144 | | Reads in one batch | 64 | | Retry tokens a key remembers | the last 16 | | Samples below one rollup cutoff | 1,024 (roll a longer history in steps by moving the cutoff forward) | | Cells kept per group by a rollup cap | 1 to 4,096 | A rollup bucket whose members would exceed the 4,096 cells of one sample is refused; use a smaller bucket. A key has one time-to-live, as every feature key does; a time-to-live per group is not provided. The in-process C-string door refuses `MergeReduce` because it cannot carry a binary value; use the proxy client. #### Measured write cost A merge-reduce write spends a fixed number of allocations whatever the cell count: 130.9 per write at 50, 150 and 1,000 cells, down from 687.8, 1,699.7 and 10,211.8 (release build, `alloc-probe` feature, 8-byte key, local measurement). Source: the `#[ignore]` measurement `a_merge_write_does_not_allocate_per_cell` and pull request #3076. This counts allocations, not latency or throughput. #### In progress Open pull request, not yet part of `main`: a typed reducer for feature aggregates (#2864). Until it merges, treat it as unavailable. The Window Reducer under its `WindowReduce*` names, its rollup command with tiers, the member set, anchor, quota, decay score, fan-in and batch reads and the retry ring described above are on `main`; the wire messages and the translator that maps them are described in [Window Reducer protocol](docs/WINDOW_REDUCE_PROTOCOL.md). The stored key tag `cells` and the retry item kind `cell_retry` keep their original spelling because they are written to disk. Feast remains a first-class integration, not a replacement for native clients. Use the [Rust SDK](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/tree/main/sdk/rust/temporalstore), [Python context SDK](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/tree/main/sdk/python), HTTP APIs, or the documented RESP surface for the corresponding workloads. The Rust memory API uses `infer=false` for explicit messages without a chat-model call. With a configured model, `infer=true` creates separate memories from extracted facts rather than cataloging raw conversations. Internal inference uses protobuf and bounded fact receipts, reusing existing entity vectors. See [inferred memory behavior and coordinated rollout](docs/MEMORY_INFERRED_FACTS.md). ## Recorded benchmark highlights Selected verified results from checked-in reports, not a new benchmark run. For a service comparison, report both rows/s and requests/s, batch size, read/write concurrency, and p50/p95/p99 latency. Keep acknowledgement policy, replication, payloads, cache budget, and storage medium explicit. A warm read-only run or an asynchronously accepted write is not a substitute for a durable mixed workload. Report physical bytes written per accepted logical byte separately from retained storage per live logical byte; expiry and reclamation change the latter over time. | Workload | Recorded result | Scope | |---|---|---| | Feature-history ingestion | **14,965-15,260 events/s** | Durable commit; 1,024 entities x 64 events; batches of 256; default 16 MiB cache | | Batched feature aggregates | **4,207 queries/s**, batch p99 **16.906 ms** | 64 queries/call; repeated runs and exact value checks | | Wide feature reads | **12,289 warm rows/s** | Async commit; 4,096 entities; 12,296 bytes/row; batch 10; isolated tmpfs; maintenance disabled | | Binary feature transport | **24.99% fewer request bytes; 4.93x faster client encoding** | Same 4,096-command, 12,296-byte-payload probe against JSON; not server throughput | | Context quality | **6.466/10 augmented**, 4.879 managed-only, 4.117 local-only | Qwen2.5 7B; four judged turns from a ten-turn experiment | These are local release-build observations, not distributed capacity or maintenance-under-load claims. Operation units and durability differ; context quality is model-judged and does not imply universal quality or token savings. Conditions, controls, and reproduction commands: [feature-serving and Feast report](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/feast_online_store_benchmark.md), [context results](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/local_context_token_quality/multiturn_3arm_multiturn_qwen7b.json), [benchmark methodology](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/README.md). ## Quick start Prerequisites: Git, Docker, and Docker Compose. ```bash git clone https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore.git cd TemporalStore docker compose -f docker-compose.single-node.yml up --build -d curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:17102/health ``` The Compose setup runs a metaserver on `17101` and a data node on `17102`. A named volume preserves data across container restarts. `/health` checks process liveness, not whether every shard can serve requests. To stop this local deployment while retaining its named data volume: ```bash docker compose -f docker-compose.single-node.yml down ``` Do not add `--volumes` when retaining data. Use the same checkout and Compose project name when starting it again so that Compose selects the existing volume. [Linux](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/linux_deploy.md) | [Windows Docker](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/windows_docker_install.md) | [macOS](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/macos_deploy.md). ## Architecture and durability TemporalStore owns temporal indexes, feature/context APIs, packed blocks, caching, persistence, and maintenance. Replicated deployments add placement and consensus. Asynchronous acceptance and confirmed persistence provide different guarantees; choose settings for the required recovery. Eligible synchronous shared-row batches release the engine mutation guard before waiting for their shared WAL commit barrier. Successful writes still wait for a barrier covering their sequence; readers can observe an in-flight update before the writer receives durable success. Read visibility alone therefore does not prove crash durability, and a commit error is not a rollback guarantee. Async, replay, Raft-application, and index-persisting paths have their own commit rules. See the [batch implementation](crates/temporalstore-rust/src/engine/stream_batch_methods.rs). Feature-write batches reuse append state and capture the slab target once per operation, rather than repeatedly checking the same configuration and directory. The next operation can observe an updated target. This reduces repeated work; it does not disable sync barriers, change the WAL format, or establish a service latency improvement. See the [append path](crates/temporalstore-rust/src/block_store/block_store_append.rs) and [storage configuration](crates/temporalstore-rust/src/storage_config.rs). Feast materialization can split one caller batch into several native requests. Do not treat that caller batch as one atomic transaction. Compare accepted rows, request counts, durability, and concurrent reader work together when evaluating batch limits; smaller requests can improve scheduling while adding WAL records and synchronization work. No universal throughput or latency win is implied. Maintenance spans preparation, checkpoint/dump, expiry, eviction, compaction, page/slab, index and WAL reclaim, delayed destruction, and restore. Both workload families require tested recovery and replication fences, plus measured per-stage CPU, memory, I/O amplification, throughput, and tail latency. This remains qualification work, not a blanket production-readiness claim. [Shared storage](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/shared_store_replication.md) | [Raft and snapshots](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/raft_replication_and_snapshots.md) | [Indexed WAL reads](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/indexed_wal_reads.md). ## Deployment boundaries - Series retention is count-based; whole-key TTL is not per-point age retention. - General aggregates can scan the requested window; accelerated paths have explicit limits. - Bounded embedding scoring is not a graph-based ANN index. The built-in hash embedding is for tests; encoder changes require compatible model identity and re-embedding. - Validate authentication, exposure, backups, replication, and acknowledgement settings before deployment. - Formats can change before a stable milestone. Pin revisions and test retained-data upgrades. The engine is Rust-native. Development targets `main`; `rust-main` is retired. There is no brpc/thrift compatibility layer. Validate production-readiness claims with deployment guides and readiness reports for the chosen configuration. ## Six open-source projects All six projects are public under **Apache-2.0**, available worldwide for anyone to use, fork, modify, test, and contribute to under the license. The storage, cache, consensus, and object-store components are Rust; MatrixArk is Python companion tooling. MatrixAdsDemo is a standalone Python demonstration using generated data. Context-management code and serving remain in TemporalStore. | Project | Role | |---|---| | [TemporalStore](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore) | Rust feature, context, and control-state serving engine | | [MatrixCache](https://github.com/matrixarkai/matrixcache) | Rust multi-layer cache | | [MatrixRaft](https://github.com/matrixarkai/matrixraft) | Rust consensus library | | [MatrixObject](https://github.com/matrixarkai/MatrixObject) | Rust distributed object storage | | [MatrixArk](https://github.com/matrixarkai/matrixark) | Optional Python ingestion, retrieval, and feedback tooling | | [MatrixAdsDemo](https://github.com/matrixarkai/MatrixAdsDemo) | Standalone ads retrieval, prediction, and auction demonstration | ## Build and contribute ```bash cargo check -p temporalstore-rust --all-targets cargo test -p temporalstore-rust --lib --tests -- --test-threads=1 cargo fmt --all -- --check ``` Development targets `main`. Anyone may open an [issue](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/issues) or [pull request](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/pulls). [Contribution guide](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) | [Code of conduct](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) | [Security policy](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/SECURITY.md). ## License [Apache License 2.0](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/LICENSE) | [NOTICE](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/NOTICE) | [Third-party notices](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md) | [Trademarks](https://github.com/matrixarkai/TemporalStore/blob/main/docs/TRADEMARKS.md).

items.name: overlay-web
items.description: The control plane for your AI employees
items.readme_text:
Overlay

Overlay is an open-source workspace where humans and AI agents share context and get work done together. Keep knowledge in one place, delegate repeatable work to agents, review what they produce, and take action through connected tools.
🔗 **[Try Overlay](https://getoverlay.io)** ## Why Overlay Most AI products stop at a single answer. Overlay is built around the next step: a person and one or more agents working in the same context. A human can set direction, provide files and memory, ask an agent to research or execute a task, inspect the result, and decide what happens next. The workspace is the shared layer between people and agents. Conversations, notes, files, projects, connected apps, and automations can be combined without moving work between separate tools. Overlay is designed to stay provider-neutral as models and agent runtimes change. ## Documentation - [Developer & self-hosting docs](docs/introduction.mdx) — local setup, runtime config, deployment, API reference. - [Quickstart](docs/developer/contribute/run-locally.mdx) — get the web app running locally. - [API Reference](docs/developer/api/overview.mdx) — generated from `src/shared/schemas/api-boundary.ts`. - [Security policy](SECURITY.md) — reporting, launch controls, and secret handling. Run `npm run docs:check` before publishing docs changes. ## Powered By
[![Vercel AI SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel%20AI%20SDK-black?logo=vercel&logoColor=white)](https://sdk.vercel.ai/docs) [![Convex](https://img.shields.io/badge/Convex-FCBD42?logo=convex&logoColor=black)](https://convex.dev) [![WorkOS](https://img.shields.io/badge/WorkOS-6366F1?logo=workos&logoColor=white)](https://workos.com) [![Stripe](https://img.shields.io/badge/Stripe-635BFF?logo=stripe&logoColor=white)](https://stripe.com) [![Composio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Composio-FF6B6B?logo=data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCAyNCAyNCIgZmlsbD0ibm9uZSIgc3Ryb2tlPSJjdXJyZW50Q29sb3IiIHN0cm9rZS13aWR0aD0iMiI+PHBhdGggZD0iTTEyIDJhMTAgMTAgMCAxIDAgMTAgMTBBMTAgMTAgMCAwIDAgMTIgMloiLz48cGF0aCBkPSJNMTIgNmE2IDYgMCAxIDAgNiA2QTYgNiAwIDAgMCAxMiA2WiIvPjwvc3ZnPg==&logoColor=white)](https://composio.dev)
| Service | Purpose | |---------|---------| | **Vercel AI SDK** | AI streaming, tool calling, multi-provider support | | **Convex** | Backend functions, data, and realtime sync | | **WorkOS** | Enterprise-grade authentication and SSO | | **Stripe** | Billing and subscription management | | **Composio** | 100+ external app integrations |
## How It Works 1. **Bring your context** — Upload files, save memories, create notes, and organize work into projects. 2. **Chat or Work** — Use Chat for conversation and synthesis; use Work when an agent needs to use tools, browse, or carry out a task. 3. **Review and continue** — Inspect sources, files, tool activity, and generated outputs, then keep working in the same shared context. ## Features See [FEATURES.md](FEATURES.md) for release status, feature flags, provider support and how to re-enable deferred features. ### Core Capabilities - **Provider-neutral Chat** — Use the model providers enabled for your deployment from one workspace - **Chat and Work modes** — Keep conversation and agent-led tool execution in the same thread - **Persistent Memory** — Save preferences, facts, and standing instructions that compound over time - **Knowledge Base** — Upload files, create folders, and search across your personal knowledge with semantic retrieval - **Project Organization** — Group chats, notes, files, and context by project for focused work - **Media Generation** — Create images and videos without leaving the workspace - **Voice Input** — Record and transcribe audio directly into notes or chat - **Browser Automation** — Run interactive browser tasks for live web work - **External Integrations** — Connect Gmail, Calendar, Notion, GitHub, and 100+ apps via Composio - **Automations** — Schedule recurring AI workflows that run on your behalf ### Workspace Areas | Area | Description | |---|---| | **Chat** | Multi-model conversations with context from memories, files, and projects | | **Notes** | Rich notebook editor with markdown, slash commands, and project linking | | **Memories** | Durable facts and preferences that shape future responses | | **Knowledge** | File storage with semantic search across documents and folders | | **Projects** | Scoped workspaces for organizing related chats, notes, and files | | **Outputs** | Gallery of generated images and videos with metadata and downloads | | **Integrations** | Connected apps and tools for external actions | | **Voice** | Audio recording and transcription flows | ### Tools & Actions #### Knowledge & Memory - **Memory CRUD** — Save, update, delete, and search personal memories - **File search** — Lexical and semantic search across uploaded documents - **Note management** — Create, edit, and organize notebook entries - **Knowledge retrieval** — Hybrid semantic + keyword search across all saved context #### Content Generation - **Image generation** — GPT Image, Grok Image, FLUX, Seedream models with aspect ratio control - **Video generation** — Veo 3.1, Seedance, Grok Video, Kling, Wan models - **Image-to-video** — Animate static images into motion clips - **Reference-to-video** — Place characters into new video scenes - **Motion control** — Transfer motion from reference video to character images - **Video editing** — Transform existing videos with text prompts #### Automation & Execution - **Browser sessions** — AI-controlled browser for interactive web tasks - **Computers** — Persistent cloud machines with a terminal, browser, and desktop for agents - **Scheduled automations** — Interval, daily, weekly, or monthly recurring workflows - **Skills** — Reusable instruction templates for common tasks - **MCP servers** — Connect external tool servers via Model Context Protocol #### Integrations (via Composio) - Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Sheets, Google Drive - Notion, Asana, Slack, GitHub - LinkedIn, X (Twitter), Outlook - And 100+ more apps ## Providers and model catalog The model catalog is intentionally not duplicated in this README. Provider names, model IDs, capabilities, availability, and pricing change independently of the application. Use the in-product model selector and the gateway metadata as the source of truth for the deployment you are running. Overlay keeps provider adapters behind a common gateway so the collaboration model remains stable while the available providers evolve. ## Built With - [Next.js 15](https://nextjs.org/) — React framework with App Router - [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) — Styling - [Vercel AI SDK](https://sdk.vercel.ai/docs) — AI streaming, tool calling, and multi-provider support - [Convex](https://convex.dev/) — Backend functions, data, and realtime sync - [WorkOS](https://workos.com/) — Enterprise authentication and SSO - [Stripe](https://stripe.com/) — Billing and subscriptions - [Composio](https://composio.dev/) — External app integrations - [TipTap](https://tiptap.dev/) — Rich text editing - [Boat](https://boat.dev/) (formerly Box) — Managed machines for Computers and agent environments - [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/) — Unified model API - [Shadcn/UI](https://ui.shadcn.com/) — UI components ## Repository Layout ```text . ├── convex/ # Backend schema, queries, mutations, actions, HTTP routes ├── src/app/ # Next.js pages, layouts, and API route handlers ├── src/features/ # Web feature containers and feature-local helpers ├── src/components/ # Shared UI primitives, layout, and providers ├── src/server/ # Server-only auth, billing, storage, AI, and route services ├── src/shared/ # Isomorphic contracts and client-safe helpers ├── packages/ # Cross-surface packages and typed API clients ├── scripts/ # Sanity scripts and one-off checks ├── docs/ # Product, setup, testing, marketing, and implementation docs ├── AGENTS.md # Local agent workspace notes ├── LICENSE # AGPL-3.0 license text └── SECURITY.md # Security policy and reporting guidance ``` ## Local Development ### Prerequisites - Node.js 22+ - npm - Convex account (dev + prod deployments) - WorkOS credentials (for auth) - Stripe test credentials (for billing) ### Quick Start ```bash # Install dependencies npm install # Configure environment cp .env.example .env.local # Edit .env.local with your credentials # Run development server npm run dev ``` For complete environment setup, see [`docs/developer/contribute/run-locally.mdx`](docs/developer/contribute/run-locally.mdx) and [`docs/self-hosting/configure/environment.mdx`](docs/self-hosting/configure/environment.mdx). ### Convex Workflow Convex deployments are environment-specific. Use `npm run convex:push:dev` only with an explicitly selected engineer-owned dev backend. Use `npm run convex:push:prod` only from a clean canonical `main` worktree after its matching web deployment is live. Feature worktrees must not deploy shared dev or customer production Convex; hosted PR builds deploy only their scoped preview backend. ## Available Commands | Command | Purpose | |---------|---------| | `npm run dev` | Run the Next.js development server | | `npm run build` | Create a production build | | `npm run convex:push:prod` | Push Convex changes to production | | `npm run convex:push:dev` | Push Convex changes to dev | ## Security - Session cookies are encrypted and signed - Transfer tokens are short-lived and hashed - Provider keys isolated behind `PROVIDER_KEYS_SECRET` - Sensitive logs redacted in chat and billing flows - See `SECURITY.md` for full security guidance ## Project status Overlay is under active development. The hosted product and the open-source repository may change as the collaboration model, provider integrations, and self-hosting support mature. Treat deployment, billing, and provider configuration as environment-specific and verify them before running a production instance. ## Contributing - Do not commit real secrets or customer data - Keep public docs on placeholders - Treat `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values as public - Prefer backend logic in `convex/` with web handlers in `src/app/api/` - Open issues and pull requests are welcome. LayerNorm requires the contributor terms in [`CLA.md`](CLA.md) before accepting an outside contribution. ## License All first-party material stored directly in this repository is licensed under `AGPL-3.0-only`. Paid commercial licenses are available separately from LayerNorm Inc. Third-party material and separate submodules retain their own licenses. - Overlay branding is governed by the trademark policy. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE), [`docs/self-hosting/licensing/license.mdx`](docs/self-hosting/licensing/license.mdx), and [`TRADEMARKS.md`](TRADEMARKS.md). --- *Overlay — A shared workspace for humans and agents.*

简体中文 · English

# GraphAgent > 跑动态工作流的终端编码智能体：主智能体自己设计依赖图，子智能体按波次并行执行，状态持久化，崩溃后能恢复。 [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent)](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/releases) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT%20%2B%20Apache--2.0-blue)](#起源与许可) [![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent)](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/stargazers) GraphAgent 是独立的终端编码智能体，专注动态 DAG 工作流。它起源于 opencode 的早期版本，从 v2.0 起完全独立维护。 单个智能体循环处理一步到位的任务没有问题。任务一旦有先后依赖、有能并行的部分、中途还要过一道审查，它就吃力了：本该并行的活被串着跑，中间结论也没人复核。进程一挂，只能从头来。GraphAgent 让主智能体先把任务画成一张依赖图，再按图执行。图不是预先写死的，是它按任务现设计的，所以 DAG 工作流基本上就是动态工作流。 图里每个节点是一个真实的子会话，有自己的智能体和上下文窗口；依赖都满足的节点算一个波次，同一波次里并行跑。状态以事件持久化，所以能暂停、单步、重规划，崩溃后按持久化的记录恢复，不会凭空重放模型调用。 ## 项目状态 v2.0 开发中，即将发布。发布进度在[里程碑](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/milestone/7)里跟踪；可复现的问题请提 [Issue](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/issues)。 ## 核心能力 | 能力 | 说明 | | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | DAG 工作流 | 主智能体设计依赖图，每个节点是真实的子会话，按波次并行；状态持久化，可暂停、恢复、重规划；节点超时从拿到执行槽位起算，排队时间不计 | | 统一子运行 | `task` 与 DAG 节点共用 ChildRun：每次委派一条持久记录，统一归属校验、取消和结果投递；子会话只接受主 agent 通信 | | 前后台委派 | 提示词准则决定 `task` 在前台等待还是后台运行；后台结果完成时以一条消息回注，不打断主会话 | | 只读 review | 内置只读 `review` agent；`/review` 默认后台执行，结论由主会话转述 | | 思考塑形 🧪 | 实验性功能，默认关闭 | | 项目记忆 | `/memory`，只保存你确认过的内容，同一项目的所有 worktree 共用 | | Goal / Loop | `/goal`、`/subgoal`，外部 judge 判断进度，有回合预算 | | 定时提醒 | `/remind`，持久化的定时提醒；会话忙时等回合结束再送达，关闭期间到期的重启后补发 | | Hooks | 兼容 Claude Code hooks 协议 | | 上下文管理 | 工具输出限制、工具调用上限、长会话压缩 | ### DAG 工作流 主智能体觉得任务值得拆，就自己建图，不用你开口；你也可以用 `/dag-auto <任务>` 直接要求。边只表示“下游要读上游的产出”，没有这层关系的节点就并行。负责审查和仲裁的节点叫门禁，输出 ACCEPT、REVISE、REJECT 或 BLOCKED，下游可以按裁定决定跑不跑。TUI 里有 DAG 检查器，能看各波次和节点的实时状态，也能进入任何一个节点的子会话。 模型分层写在 `.agents/settings.json` 的 `dag.model`（判断、验收和评审节点用 advanced，写代码和探索这类跑量的用 standard），常用的图存进 `.agents/workflows/`，之后按名字就能启动。精选模板在 [opencode-dag-config](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/opencode-dag-config)。节点的 `timeout_ms` 从拿到执行槽位开始计时，排队时间不计。崩溃恢复只认持久化的记录。引擎不假设有跨进程的锁，也不保证节点恰好执行一次。用法和引擎细节见 [docs/dag-workflows.md](./docs/dag-workflows.md)。 ### 子运行与通信 `task` 和 DAG 节点共用同一套 ChildRun。一次委派对应一条持久记录，记录归属、状态与结算结果；后台运行结束后结果只投递一次，重启或进程丢失的运行也会补投。子会话不接受自由输入：HTTP 操作层对子会话的写请求返回 409，只放行权限回复和只读旁问；引擎准入要求携带当前运行的 live 凭证。 `agent` 工具负责主会话与 DAG 节点之间的观察和消息：`observe` 分页查看节点进度与尝试，`send` 向确切的活跃尝试投递，`receive` 读取邮箱。节点需要澄清时问父会话，不直接问用户。工具只在存在活跃 DAG 节点运行时出现，可见性由进程内注册表判定，不查数据库。 ### 只读 review 与前后台分类 `/review` 使用内置的只读 `review` agent：它能读文件、搜索、查 LSP、跑只读的 git 和 forge 命令，不能编辑文件、起子任务或跑会改文件的命令。命令默认在后台运行，结束后把结论交回主会话，由主会话转述。 `task` 的前台/后台由提示词里的准则判断，代码不做启发式分类。默认走前台；需要用户输入或确认、会影响与主会话共享的状态、结果是下一步的直接输入、或是主会话能直接回答的快速查询时，一律走前台。同时满足以下几点才走后台：你表示会同时做别的事（“同时”“不用等”这类说法）或明确要求后台；委派的工作只读，或只写你和主会话都不会碰的文件；结果一条消息能说完。此时主会话先委派、不预先调查，再继续你同时要求的前台工作；没有剩余才简短回复并结束回合，结果稍后以一条消息送回。agent 或命令可以声明执行方式（`execution`），声明优先于提示词准则；交互型 agent 恒前台。理由和评测结果见 [ADR 0003](./docs/adr/0003-task-execution-classification.md)。 ### 思考塑形 🧪 实验性功能，默认关闭。思考型模型会把之前的思考内容在后续请求里回传，里面常有复述、被推翻的猜测和纠错过程。这个功能在后台把已完成的思考整理得更短，在后续步骤的请求里换用整理后的版本。整理失败、超时或没有可用的小模型时保留原文；原文一直存着，关掉功能后回放的就是原文。带签名或加密的思考不会碰。 我们想知道的是，开源模型的思考内容经过塑形之后，输出能力会不会提高。效果还在验证，所以标成实验性、默认关闭。整理用配置的 `small_model`，没配就用服务商自带的小模型： ```jsonc // graphagent.json { "small_model": "provider/small-model", // 建议选有 `none` 推理档位的模型 "reasoningDistillation": { "enabled": true, // 显式开启；默认 false }, } ``` ### 项目记忆 `/memory on` 开启后，GraphAgent 按项目保存偏好、决策和术语，只保存经你确认的内容，同一项目的所有 worktree 共用一份。它不是代码索引，也不会压过你当前的输入和更高优先级的指令。 ### Goal 与 Loop `/goal <目标>` 让智能体在当前会话里跨回合自己推进一个目标，`/subgoal` 管子目标。每个回合结束后由外部 judge 判断进度：done 就收工，continue 就接着跑。总回合数有预算（默认 20），用尽后暂停，可以恢复。目标状态持久化，重启不丢。 ### 定时提醒 `/remind` 给当前会话设一个提醒。到点时，提醒会作为一条消息送进这个会话，由智能体转告你： ```text /remind 30m 看一下 CI 结果 /remind 2h 回复评审意见 /remind 09:00 站会前同步进度 /remind 明天 09:00 发周报 /remind every 1h 起身活动一下 /remind list /remind cancel rmd_1a2b3c4d ``` - `30m`、`2h`：从现在起的时长，单位只有 `m`（分钟）和 `h`（小时）。 - `09:00`：当天的这个钟点，已经过了就取明天；`明天 09:00`（也可以写 `tomorrow 09:00`）是明天的这个钟点。钟点按本机时区算。 - `every 1h`：重复提醒，首次在一个间隔之后，之后每隔一个间隔一次；间隔最短 5 分钟。 - `/remind list` 列出本会话待触发的提醒，`/remind cancel ` 取消一个。id 形如 `rmd_xxxxxxxx`，创建时的回执和 `list` 里都有。 提醒是持久化的，重启不丢，会话删除时一并删除。到点时如果会话空闲就送达，正忙就等当前回合结束后再送达；每次到期只送达一次。GraphAgent 关闭期间到期的提醒，下次在这个会话所在的目录启动时补发一次；重复提醒只补最近的一次，之后仍按原来的节奏。送达时比计划晚了一分钟以上，消息里会标明晚了多久。提醒文本原样放进这条消息，消息里要求智能体先告诉你，文本若是要做的事就接着做。 提醒只能由你用这条命令创建，模型没有创建提醒的工具；它只适用于主会话，在子会话里会被拒绝。 ### Hooks 兼容 Claude Code 的 hooks 协议。`hooks.json` 从全局配置目录和项目的 `.agents` 目录读取，执行类型有 command、HTTP、MCP 工具、prompt 和 agent 五种；项目里的 hooks 要先经过信任确认才会生效。`/import-claude` 把 `.claude/settings*.json` 审阅后转换进 `.agents/`，`/create-hook` 带你写新的 hook。详细说明见 [hooks 指南](./packages/graphagent/src/skill/builtin/configure-hooks.md)。 ### 上下文管理 一组管上下文的功能：限制工具输出的长度、限制每次输入的工具调用次数、自动压缩长会话。截断输出时会给出可执行的续读方式。 ## 其他改动 - `task` 可以按 `task_id` 续接子智能体；后台子智能体完成时自动通知。 - 所有模型共用一份系统提示词，工具的用法写在各自的描述里，不按 Provider 挑提示词。 - 工具更严格，也更容易排错：`edit` 严格匹配（多处命中时列出候选行，找不到时给出最接近的片段），参数校验的报错带字段级提示。 - 支持用独立的 git worktree 管理工作目录。工作流不会自动隔离，并发的工作流要用不同的 worktree，或者串行跑。 - 会话创建时可指定 DAG 模式；TUI 页脚显示开关状态，状态接口返回可用性、并发与节点上限、token 预算用量。 - `config_assistant`（命令 `ocfg`）是一个用 Go 写的独立 TUI，用来定位、校验和编辑配置。 ## 快速开始 预构建的二进制（Linux、macOS，附 SHA256SUMS）在 [Releases](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/releases) 页，解压后把 `graphagent` 放进 PATH，在项目目录里运行。v2.0 起不再发布 Windows 原生版本，也不再运行 Windows 集成测试；Windows 用户请安装 WSL，在 WSL 中按 Linux 方式安装使用。仓库里现有的 `oc` 安装脚本会在 v2.1 删除，安装和升级都并入主程序，见路线图。GraphAgent 不发布到 npm、brew 和 scoop，上游的 `opencode-ai` 装的是上游 opencode，不是 GraphAgent。 从源码运行需要 `package.json` 里 `packageManager` 固定的 Bun，以及 `.node-version` 指定的 Node： ```bash bun install bun dev <项目目录> # 启动 TUI；不带目录时在 packages/graphagent 里运行 ``` 启动之后，给它一件有阶段、有并行空间的活就行，不用先写任何 DAG 配置： ```text /dag-auto 把 auth 和 server 两个包迁移到新 API，最后跑集成测试 ``` 想把常用的图固定下来，就存成 `.agents/workflows/parallel-migrate.yaml`，之后说一句“跑 parallel-migrate 工作流”就按名字启动。下面这份 spec 里，两个迁移节点在同一波次并行，`assemble` 等它们都完成才开始： ```yaml title: 并行迁移 config: name: parallel-migrate nodes: - id: discover name: discover worker_type: explore depends_on: [] required: true prompt_template: { inline: "列出所有需要迁移到新 API 的包。" } - id: migrate-auth name: migrate-auth worker_type: build depends_on: [discover] prompt_template: { inline: "把 auth 包迁移到新 API。" } - id: migrate-server name: migrate-server worker_type: build depends_on: [discover] prompt_template: { inline: "把 server 包迁移到新 API。" } - id: assemble name: assemble worker_type: build depends_on: [migrate-auth, migrate-server] prompt_template: { inline: "跑集成测试，汇总结果。" } ``` 安装步骤、完整性校验和源码构建的细节见 [docs/install.md](./docs/install.md)。 ## 设计思路 我们把图当成一份可执行、可持久化、可检查的契约，不是给人看的流程图，也不是事后给提示词链加的箭头。边必须真的传递产出：下游不读上游的东西，这条依赖就该删，独立的工作直接并行。模板只是参考拓扑，主智能体可以按任务增删分支，但每次剪枝要写明理由。预测、复审和裁决由不同的角色做，门禁不能剪。迭代只是有界的局部改图，不存在隐藏的环。最后，代码和测试说了算，状态靠事件记录恢复，代价高的地方留给人暂停、单步、取消和重规划。 第一个完整的 DAG 引擎提交是 2026-07-02；论文 [What makes prompts a graph](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27578) 到 2026-07-30 才把显式结构、提示词与拓扑分离、可执行语义和“图是一等制品”这些想法归纳出来，比引擎晚了四周。 ## 路线图 v2.0 的剩余工作也在[里程碑](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/milestone/7)里跟踪： - DAG 模式的行为面：并发池、预算与质量机制、节点权限自动裁决。 - workflow 工具接口收敛、工作流级 worktree、事件驱动邮箱与持久对账。 - agent 契约与 composer：内置调研、架构设计、原型设计 agent，并在 DAG 内组合公共 agent。 - PR 监听改为事件源；`/remind` 持久提醒；后台任务显示与子 agent 只读界面。 - v2.0.0 发布：版本推导、Breaking 清单、中英迁移指南与 Linux、macOS 冒烟。 - v2.1：安装与升级并入主程序，直接从 GitHub 检索新版本并升级，不再需要 `oc` 脚本；release 打包随之调整，macOS 上安装不用再输密码；配置也可以从 GitHub 仓库读取（[#1281](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/issues/1281)）。 这些都是计划，实际状态以里程碑为准。 ## 起源与许可 GraphAgent 起源于早期的 opencode（MIT，[anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode)），从 v2.0 起作为独立项目维护。 许可分两条：继承自上游的代码保持 MIT，包括被我们改过的上游文件，文本见 [LICENSE](./LICENSE)；GraphAgent 新写的代码是 Apache-2.0，文本见 [LICENSE-APACHE](./LICENSE-APACHE)。精确的文件边界在 [LICENSE-UPSTREAM.txt](./LICENSE-UPSTREAM.txt)，[NOTICE](./NOTICE) 有摘要。再分发时请保留 NOTICE 里的版权与归属声明。 ## 文档 除 architecture.md 和功能清单外，下面的文档目前只有英文。 - [docs/architecture.md](./docs/architecture.md)：v1 架构，包括组件与目录、客户端与协议、源码索引 - [docs/dag-workflows.md](./docs/dag-workflows.md)：DAG 工作流的用法、配置和引擎细节 - [docs/install.md](./docs/install.md)：安装、完整性校验和源码构建 - [docs/compaction-retry.md](./docs/compaction-retry.md)：Provider 重试与压缩请求 - [hooks 指南](./packages/graphagent/src/skill/builtin/configure-hooks.md)：事件、配置和验证方法 - [docs/功能清单.md](./docs/功能清单.md)：功能与源码入口索引 - [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md)：开发指南 - [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md)：贡献说明 ## 链接 [GitHub](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent) · [Issues](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/issues) · [Releases](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/releases) · [里程碑](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/milestone/7) · [opencode-dag-config](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/opencode-dag-config)

items.name: bike4mind
items.description: The open-core AI workbench — notebooks, agents, RAG, voice, and images across any model: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, or local via Ollama/vLLM. BSL 1.1, auto-converting to Apache-2.0 on a two-year clock. Your AI keeps running when theirs doesn't.
items.readme_text:
# Bike4Mind **Your bicycle for the mind in the age of AI.** An open-core AI knowledge platform — a multi-model workspace where notebooks, autonomous agents, and a RAG knowledge engine work together to augment any cognitive task. [![Chat on Bike4Mind](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-Bike4Mind-6d28d9)](https://app.bike4mind.com) [![License: BUSL-1.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-BUSL--1.1-blue)](./LICENSE) [![Discussions](https://img.shields.io/badge/community-Discussions-24292f)](https://github.com/bike4mind/bike4mind/discussions) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/bike4mind/bike4mind?style=flat&label=stars&color=6d28d9)](https://github.com/bike4mind/bike4mind)
--- ## What is Bike4Mind? Bike4Mind is an AI-powered knowledge platform that wires a superset of AI technologies together behind one workspace. Bring your own models, keep your data, and let agents do the heavy lifting. - **Notebooks** — the core workspace: chat, documents, and context in one place, across any model. - **Multi-LLM by design** — swap freely between **Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, xAI, Ollama** (local), and more, plus image models (GPT-Image-2, Nano Banana, FLUX). - **Quest Master** — autonomous, multi-step task planning: text and image generation, vision review, web search, math, code, and human-in-the-loop steps, run in parallel. - **AI Agents** — autonomous ReAct-style agents that carry out complex tasks against your tools and knowledge. - **Knowledge Engine** — RAG over your documents: smart chunking, vector search, collections, and tagging so agents can reason about what you know. - **Artifacts** — reusable snippets, documents, and visualizations produced by agents, with a built-in publish-and-share layer. Try the hosted service at **[app.bike4mind.com](https://app.bike4mind.com)**, or self-host the open core on your own infrastructure (below). ## Open core Bike4Mind is **open core**. The engine is public and self-hostable; the multi-tenant hosted service is our business. - **Open** (this repo, BUSL-1.1): the agent engine, LLM adapters, CLI, data models, and the self-host path — published as `@bike4mind/*` packages. - **Commercial / closed**: operating the multi-tenant hosted service — billing, entitlements, hosted infrastructure — and premium overlays such as Overwatch. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md#the-openclosed-boundary) for the exact open/closed boundary. ## Quickstart **Hosted (fastest):** sign in at **[app.bike4mind.com](https://app.bike4mind.com)** — nothing to install. **Self-host:** run the open core on your own hardware with Docker — no AWS account or cloud provider required. See the **[Self-Host Quickstart](./SELF_HOST.md)**. In short: ```bash # 1. Copy the env template, then generate JWT_SECRET / SESSION_SECRET / # SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY (see SELF_HOST.md) and add your model keys cp .env.selfhost.example .env.selfhost # 2. Bring up the stack (app + MongoDB + object storage + queues + mail catcher) docker compose -f compose.selfhost.yaml --env-file .env.selfhost up -d ``` Bike4Mind then runs at `http://localhost:3000`; sign-in code emails land in the bundled Mailpit at `http://localhost:8025`. The self-host image is published to `ghcr.io/bike4mind/bike4mind-selfhost`. ## Develop Bike4Mind is a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo (Node 24). ```bash pnpm i -r # install pnpm turbo:core:build # build the @bike4mind/* core packages pnpm turbo:typecheck # type check pnpm turbo:test # run tests ``` Project layout: `apps/client` (Next.js SPA + pages API backend), `packages/cli` (interactive CLI + ReAct agent), `b4m-core/*` (the `@bike4mind/*` engine packages), `packages/database` (Mongoose models + migrations). Realtime WebSocket fanout ships as a separate `@bike4mind/subscriber-fanout` image. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for the full guide. Building an app that signs users in with Bike4Mind and bills AI usage to their accounts? See [Building an app on Bike4Mind](docs-site/docs/developers/building-on-b4m.md). ## Contributing Contributions are welcome — fork → topic branch → PR → squash-merge. All contributors sign a lightweight CLA on their first PR (you keep your copyright). Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) and our [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Questions and self-hosting help go in [Discussions](https://github.com/bike4mind/bike4mind/discussions). ## Security Please report vulnerabilities privately — see [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md). Do not open public issues for security problems. ## License Bike4Mind is licensed under the **[Business Source License 1.1](./LICENSE)** with a broad Additional Use Grant: - ✅ You **may** read, modify, redistribute, and make production use of the code — including self-hosting it for your organization's own internal use, and building or commercializing your own products on top of it. - ❌ You **may not** offer the software to third parties as a competing hosted/managed service (a "Bike4Mind Service", as defined in the LICENSE). - 🕓 Each released version **converts to Apache-2.0** two years after its public release. This license will never be tightened. For alternative licensing, contact **licensing@bike4mind.com**. © 2026 Bike4Mind, Inc.
